hens_rule_text: Chicago has no chicken-specific ordinance: hens may be kept for eggs or as pets with no numeric limit, subject to general nuisance, noise, sanitation and animal care rules.
permit_notes: No city permit for keeping hens was found in Chapter 7-12; local chicken groups also report none.
setback_notes: No chicken-specific setback found in the city code.
coop_rules: General sanitation, humane housing and noise rules apply; animals may not make excessive noise.
zoning_notes: Sec. 7-12-300 bans keeping any animal for your own food or slaughtering it, except in licensed establishments; eggs are expressly exempt. A 2023 proposal (O2023-0002993) to cap hens at 6, ban roosters and require a permit was reported, but no evidence it passed was found.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Read Sec. 7-12-300 via Internet Archive copy. The absence of a hen limit, permit or rooster ban rests on the code having no chicken-specific rule, reported by secondary sources; status of the 2023 livestock ordinance proposal could not be confirmed.
